On Linux with Xfce, Ghostty seemed locked into a GNOME-like look with header bars and client-side decorations. The user could not swap these for standard title bars and menus, which left it inconsistent with the rest of their desktop.

Workaround to blend in with XFCE: set 'window-theme = system', 'gtk-titlebar = false', 'gtk-wide-tabs = false' and 'gtk-adwaita = false' in the config. Another user replied: 'Thanks, ghostty looked really off in KDE by default.'

After testing Ghostty, one user found higher input lag than xfce4-terminal, blurrier fonts and 3–4x the memory footprint, and the UI was still less consistent with their desktop. 'Disabling the UI cruft just turns it into a less performant version of Xterm... this is going to be an uninstall for me.'

Building on Debian/Ubuntu failed with a glib-compile-resources error until the user installed libgtk-4-dev and libadwaita-1-dev. They were surprised there's no .deb package. Another user noted the GTK4 in Ubuntu 22.04 is too old to build it.

On NixOS, using Ghostty's provided flake took '60 seconds to update config and 8 minutes of actually building on a slow machine.' Another user said building from source on Debian/Ubuntu is 'quite trivial.'

Praise for the minimum-contrast option: 'I've grown so sick of tools/TUIs that output unreadable text... I look forward to never manually theming a terminal app again!' Another user said the selection-foreground/background config 'makes a massive difference.'
'I enjoy it, and it's great to have another modern high performance terminal as an option for macOS and Linux.' This user still felt Kitty has the edge, with WezTerm also a strong contender.
A 240Hz user seriously tried Ghostty but went back to their previous terminal. On their machine they could notice a small end-to-end latency between keypress and action.
A latency-sensitive user disputed an old benchmark: 'there's no way Ghostty has 41ms.' They said a newer ~13ms average 'feels about right to me. Not perfect but acceptable.'
On throughput, such as accidentally cat-ing a large file, one user said Ghostty 'performs very well... among the same league as Alacritty and Ptyxis.'
'It feels amazing on linux. I find it very noticably better than konsole.' The user said Foot and Alacritty also feel great but lack some of Ghostty's features.
Complaint: SSH didn't work out of the box because of Ghostty's own TERM value. 'If I install a terminal and SSH doesn't work from it out of the box, I would describe that as a bug.'
SSH workarounds from users: one added 'Host * SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color' to their SSH config. Another distributed xterm-ghostty.terminfo via Salt and ran 'tic -x xterm-ghostty.terminfo'.

One user keeps Ghostty open but uses iTerm2 for almost everything. Even after hacking TERM, arrow keys sometimes print escape codes until they restart. 'It's just enough friction to keep me away.' Another said SSH breaks 'more often than not' versus iTerm which 'just works.'
One user called the quick terminal feature 'ghostty's killer feature for me.' Another user wished for tmux -CC (control mode) support.

'Ghostty is awesome and I almost dropped iTerm for it until I hit cmd-f and nothing happened.' Another said: 'Missing search and weird ssh control character issues are my blockers. It's great otherwise!'
For SSH problems, a user pointed to Ghostty's terminfo docs (ghostty.org/docs/help/terminfo#ssh). Following them 'solved my issue with using htop in an ssh session.'
One user is waiting for drag-and-drop on KDE, which currently only works on GNOME. 'Although Ghostty is great I'm not going to switch to GNOME just for a terminal emulator.'
'Missing scrollbars. That and ctrl f are my two annoyances, apart from that I love ghostty and use it daily at work.'
A user switched back to Warp because Ghostty 'was a little too barebones for my use case.' Tip: Ghostty's default scrollback buffer is only ~10MB but can be changed with a config option.
